result:
status: done
checks:
- Skill security-review (built-in; the loaded text was the built-in's). Its git status showed a clean main checkout with only .holyagent state files and an empty diff against origin/HEAD, so it covered none of 675a95e..63aa076. I reviewed the range from allow-review.diff and the full shell.ts and hook.ts in /home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent-fix-cli-and-vcs. I have no shell and no sub-task tool, so I ran no tests or exploits and traced every command below by hand, with bash, git and gh behaviour taken from documented semantics, not from a run. -> exit 0
blockers:
- OPEN N7 (validated by trace; confidence high). Brace expansion, which the scan never marks as computed, hides the options the per-program guards look for. Only `$`, a substitution or a backtick sets EXPANDED, so `isDynamic` is false for `{a,b}`. Path to the sink: `find . -maxdepth 0 {-exec,sh} -c 'git commit --allow-empty -m x' ';'`. The words are `{-exec,sh}`, `-c`, one quoted `git commit ...` word and `;`. shell.ts 525-526 tests `^-(?:exec|execdir|ok|okdir|delete)$` against the literal `{-exec,sh}`, which does not match, and `args.some(isGit)` (797) sees no bare `git` word. The result is []. Bash expands it to `find . -maxdepth 0 -exec sh -c '...' ;` and a commit is made. The same shape defeats `mise {exec,--} sh -c 'git commit ...'` (guard 552-553), `bun {-e,'<code that spawns git commit>'}` (554-560), `sort --compress-{program,program}=...` (542-546), `rg {--pre,x}` (547), `test {-v,x}` (549) and `gh {alias,set} ...` (563). The docs promise that a computed word in the arguments of these programs is unclear, but only `$` forms are. Fix: set the dynamic mark on any unquoted `{...}` containing a comma or `..`, on unquoted glob characters and on a leading `~` in every word, or treat those as unclear for all guarded programs. The program word is already safe: `PLAIN_PROGRAM` rejects braces.
- OPEN N8 (validated by trace; confidence about 85% on gh's browser handling, which I could not run). `RISKY_VARIABLE` (shell.ts 442-443) is a denylist of variable names, and `BROWSER`, `GH_BROWSER`, `GH_PAGER`, `GH_EDITOR`, `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH`, `MISE_*`, `BUN_*`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `SHELLOPTS` and `PS4` are not on it. Source: the command text. Sink: gh launches the configured browser as a program, appending the URL. Command: `GH_BROWSER='git commit --allow-empty -m' gh browse`. The assignment is not risky and `gh` has no guard hit, because `GH_RUNNERS` holds only alias, extension, ext, codespace and cs, so the result is []. gh then runs `git commit --allow-empty -m <url>`. The same effect is persistent and needs no environment variable: `gh config set browser 'git commit --allow-empty -m'` passes, and a later `gh browse` or `gh pr view --web` does not mention git at all, so the `if` rule never starts the hook. Also, `gh extensions ...` (the plural alias of `gh extension`, which I recall from gh's cobra definition) is not in `GH_RUNNERS`: `gh extensions install owner/gh-x && gh x # git commit` passes and runs downloaded code. Fix: refuse any assignment prefix except a short allowlist of harmless names, or at least the gh, mise, bun, npm, node, ripgrep and shell-startup families. Add the plural `extensions` and `codespaces` to `GH_RUNNERS`, and treat `gh config set` as unclear.
- OPEN N9 (validated by trace; confidence high for the editor key, which git runs through the shell). `git config` is judged by `RISKY_CONFIG` (shell.ts 653-654), a denylist that omits many keys that start a program or change a push. Command: `git config sequence.editor 'git commit --allow-empty -m' && git rebase -i HEAD~1`. `sequence.editor` does not match the regex, no argument is the bare word `git`, `rebase` is on the list and only `-x` and `--exec` are refused, so the result is []. Git runs the editor through the shell with the todo path appended, which makes the todo path the commit message, and a commit is made. Other unlisted keys: `diff.external`, `diff.*.textconv`, `filter.*.clean/smudge`, `merge.*.driver`, `mergetool.*.cmd`, `gpg.program`, `gpg.ssh.program`, `core.askPass`, `core.gitProxy`, `pager.*`, `remote.*.receivepack` and `remote.*.uploadpack`. A force push needs no config key at all: `git remote add --mirror=push m <url> && git push m`. `git remote` is on the list with no argument check, and `git push m` is a plain push to `pushVerdict`, while the mirror setting makes it overwrite and delete remote refs. Fix: make `git config` (and `git remote add/set-*`) allowlist-only, for example reads (`--get`, `--list`, `user.*`) pass and every write is unclear.
- OPEN N10 (validated by trace; confidence about 85%, the arithmetic evaluation of a variable's value is bash behaviour I did not run). B2 is only partly closed. `skipHeredocs` (shell.ts 99) marks an unquoted heredoc body unclear only for `$(` or a backtick, but the docs promise `$[` too. A body can run a command without either: first an assignment, `x='a[$(git commit -m x)]'`, which passes because it is one literal word with no program. Then `cat <<EOF` with the body line `$[x]` and a closing `EOF`. Bash expands the body, evaluates `x` as an arithmetic expression and runs the array subscript's command substitution. `${y[x]}`, `${!x}`, `${y:x}` and `${x@P}` (prompt expansion runs `$(...)`) in the body work the same. The body is dropped unread and the result is []. The same forms outside a heredoc are already unclear (`scanBraced`, `$[`, `ARITHMETIC`). Fix: for an unquoted heredoc, scan the body as a double-quoted string, or mark unclear on `$[`, `${` and `$((`.
- OPEN N11 (validated by trace for bunx; the bun --eval= form is a suspicion). `bunx` is on the allowlist and its guard (shell.ts 561) refuses only a computed word, while the `git` check (797) refuses only a word that is exactly `git` or ends in `/git`. `bunx concurrently 'git commit --allow-empty -m x'` has one quoted word that is not `git`, so the result is []. The same holds for any package that runs a string: `bunx npm-run-all`, `bunx tsx -e`, and so on. The registry download is the sink, so no file has to exist beforehand. `mise run`, `bun run` and `bun <file>` are the documented script residual. Suspicion: the `bun` guard (554-560) matches `-e` and `--eval` exactly, so `bun --eval='Bun.spawnSync(["git","commit"])'` may pass if bun accepts the `=` form; I could not check that. Fix: drop `bunx` from PROGRAMS (the one use in the tests is `bunx lefthook install`), or allow it only for named packages, and match `^(-e|--eval|-p|--print)(=|$)`.
notes:
- Non-blocking, same class as the documented residual but now reachable inside a single allowed command. The allowlist includes writers: `echo`/`printf`/`cat` with redirections (targets are not read), `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `touch`, `mkdir`, `sed -i` and `awk`. `mv .git/hooks/pre-rebase.sample .git/hooks/post-checkout && echo '#!/bin/sh' ... > .git/hooks/post-checkout` leaves an executable hook, because the redirect keeps the mode, and the next `git checkout` makes the commit. `echo '[alias]...' >> .git/config` defines an alias that a later `git ci` uses without reaching the hook. `cp evil "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/holyagent" && "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/holyagent" # git commit` passes, since the wrapper is trusted by its text and by a path comparison at hook time only. docs/hooks.md already says `.git/` edits are not stopped, but its claim that only a known program with exact words passes cannot hold beside these writers. Say so in the docs, or make the redirect targets and the targets of cp, mv, sed -i and rm unclear when they are under `.git`, `.holyagent` or the plugin folder.
- Non-blocking: the scan's sentinel characters can be forged. A literal U+E001 typed in a command is read as `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, so a word of U+E001 plus `/scripts/holyagent` passes as the wrapper while bash runs a relative path with that name. A path-qualified `git` (`./git`, `/tmp/x/git`) is treated as git and judged by `gitVerdict` without being checked to be git. Both need a file written earlier. Fix: reject the two private-use characters in the raw command, and accept a path for git only when it resolves to a real git.
- Non-blocking: `awk -E file` and `--exec file` (gawk) are not in the awk guard (shell.ts 540), which blocks `-f`, `--file`, `-i` and `-l` but not the other ways to load a program from a file. This needs a file written earlier.
- Non-blocking: `gh api` (contents or git/refs endpoints, including a PATCH of a ref with force), `gh pr merge`, `git update-ref`, `git cherry-pick`, `git revert`, `git am`, `git pull` and `git merge` create commits or move refs without running `git commit` or a flagged push. This matches the stated decision to leave them plain Git and gh, but the objective sentence 'no history-rewriting push passes' holds only for the `git push` spellings.
- Closed with reason, r-i65u.json: N1 CLOSED (`isDynamic(first)` or `!PLAIN_PROGRAM` gives unclear, shell.ts 789; `{git,commit}` fails the plain test). N2 CLOSED (`ARITHMETIC` refuses letters, so `((git commit) && (true))` is unclear, 61-68 and 251-263). N3 CLOSED (`time -p`, `/usr/bin/time`, coproc, function, trap, source, `.`, fakeroot, xargs, mise exec and docker are unknown programs or guarded, 455-492 and 552). N4 CLOSED (`env` with any option, `timeout` and `bash -c -x` are unclear, 774-777 and 794). N5 CLOSED (`${x:1<<2 }` is unclear via `scanBraced`, and `a[1<<2 ]` via line 377). N6 CLOSED for the cited forms (`export` is unknown, and `git config alias.*` is refused by `RISKY_CONFIG`), but the same class stays open through other config keys (N9) and `.git` writes (first note).
- Closed with reason, r-28nh.json: B1 CLOSED (a decoded NUL sets unclear, shell.ts 235). B2 PARTLY CLOSED (the `$(` and backtick forms are unclear, but `$[x]`, `${y[x]}`, `${!x}` and `${x@P}` in an unquoted heredoc body are open, N10). B3 CLOSED (`$[`, `${...}` offsets, `a[1<<2 ]`, a `<<` with no delimiter-shaped word and `((` anywhere are unclear or skipped, 130-131, 147-152 and 328-333). B4 CLOSED (backslash-newline is dropped inside double quotes, 143-146). B5 CLOSED (`ARITHMETIC` rejects `$`, backticks, quotes, `;` and letters). The earlier non-blocking wrapper, nested-backtick, dynamic-subcommand and `--config-env` shapes are now unclear.
- Sound, no finding: the gate `MENTIONS_GIT_WRITE` (a superset of the host rule, case-insensitive) in hook.ts; fail-closed handling (an exception from `gitWrites` or `realpathSync` becomes a deny); the own-wrapper check (a copy, a missing path, `./scripts/holyagent` and a link to something else are unclear, and a link to the real wrapper resolves to the wrapper itself); `CLAUDE_*` assignments and `env CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=...` (refused); `git -c` limited to `SAFE_SETTING` with an exact `name=` prefix; `--exec`, `--receive-pack`, `--upload-pack` and `grep -O` with prefix matching; `rebase -x`; push flags, abbreviations, refspecs and `$'...'` decoding; `sed` e-command and `-f` patterns; `awk` system, getline and pipe; `find -exec/-ok/-delete` written literally; `sort --compress-program` prefixes; `rg --pre`; `test -v/-R` and `printf -v`; process substitution `<(...)` and `>(...)` bodies are scanned as commands; `time`, `!`, `{`, `then` and `do` handling; the `for` special case. Residuals taken as accepted: user git aliases, host `if` matching on raw text.
- Unverified: S1 (whether the host `if` globs match a multi-line command) and every bash, git, gh and bun behaviour above, because I had no shell. The tree at /home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent-fix-cli-and-vcs belongs to another worker and may have been changing; shell.ts matched the diff when read. I took no part in the repair.
